description.value: This study examined gray matter volume differences between recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls and whether left inferior frontal gyrus volume was related to stop-signal task performance.

spans.text: Therefore, the goal of our study was to investigate whether GMV differences in AD patients relative to healthy controls were related to task performance on a stop-signal task.

value: we hypothesized that prefrontal GMV would be reduced in AD patients compared with a matched sample of healthy control (HC) participants
we expected that a lower volume of prefrontal areas would be related to poor response inhibition (i.e., high SSRTs) and faster reaction times on go trials

to explore whether GMV differences and response inhibition were related to the toxic effects of alcohol, we performed additional correlation analyses for these measures and the lifetime alcohol intake of each participant in the AD patient group only

Participants responded as quickly and accurately as possible to left- or right-pointing arrows on go trials and inhibited the prepared motor response when an arrow flipped upwards on stop trials. The task comprised two blocks with 80 go trials and 20 stop trials per block, using an adaptive staircase procedure for the stop-signal delay.

instructions.value: Respond as quickly and accurately as possible; inhibit the prepared response when the stop signal appears.
